deals.evidence: The Clippers announced that the newly formed CAPSS LLC reached the agreement with The Madison Square Garden Company, which owned the Forum, to purchase the music venue for $400 million in cash.
deals.headline: Ballmer buys the Forum from MSG for $400m in cash
deals.summary: Ballmer's newly formed CAPSS LLC bought the Forum in Inglewood from MSG, settling the litigation blocking the Clippers' new arena; resolution of the litigation was a condition of the sale.

deals.evidence: funded the arena with the help of a 23-year naming-rights deal with Intuit worth $500 million
deals.headline: Intuit's 23-year, $500m naming-rights deal helps fund the privately financed Intuit Dome
deals.summary: The $2bn Intuit Dome opened in August 2024 with no state money; Ballmer funded it with the help of Intuit's naming-rights deal.

notes: Revenue, operating income, player expenses and gate receipts are Forbes estimates for 2024-25 (calculated October 2025); the team publishes no accounts. Not found: Ballmer's exact percentage or any minority/institutional holders, chief executive/president of business operations, legal entity, attendance, social follower counts. The 2014 purchase predates the brief's 2015 deal window, so it is recorded on the owner row only. The Forum deal date is from ESPN's March 2020 story (date_text only). Intuit Dome cost: Forbes 'Cost To Build $2,000M'.
